column4: The threat سَنَسِمُهُۥ عَلَى ٱلْخُرْطُومِ is the Qur'an's literal act of branding a person; it turns the section's identifying livestock mark into the visible judgment of a character.
Hoarded gold and silver are heated in Hell and used to cauterize foreheads, sides, and backs; the very worldly thing chosen becomes the fire-brand carried on the chooser's body.

ٱلْخَيْلِ ٱلْمُسَوَّمَةِ places marked or branded horses inside the adornments of worldly life, then calls all of them temporary enjoyment; it joins the section's animal brand directly to its reading of preferring الدنيا.
The stones that punish Lot's people are مُسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ, marked at or by the Lord; mark, Lord, ownership, and judgment coincide in one phrase.
مُسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ again describes the stones assigned to the transgressors, making the divine owner's identifying mark also a designation of destination.
سِيمَاهُمْ فِى وُجُوهِهِم مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلسُّجُودِ is the section's positive face-mark exactly: worship leaves an أثر by which the Lord's companions are known.
لِلْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ names those who discern signs in the overturned city; the reader of a brand becomes the reader of judgment from a ruin's surviving trace.
Satan's command that people slit the ears of livestock stages the section's exact alternative to cautery for marking an animal, while exposing a mark that falsely alters God's creation.
Sacrificial camels are called God's شعائر and His name is pronounced over them; livestock, a belonging-sign, and the owner's name meet without the need for a burned brand.
صِبْغَةَ ٱللَّهِ presents God's dye or coloring as an identity of worship and belonging, a close nonlexical counterpart to the Lord's mark borne by His own.
وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوا۟ وَءَاثَارَهُمْ says both deeds sent ahead and the traces they leave are written; choice therefore survives as an attributable أثر after the actor.
رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ makes earned conduct a coating on the heart, a precise inner version of the section's claim that preference leaves its mark on the person.
يُعْرَفُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيمَاهُمْ makes criminals known by their marks before they are seized, realizing the section's definition of a sign that distinguishes its bearer.
فَلَعَرَفْتَهُم بِسِيمَاهُمْ says the hypocrites could be recognized by their marks and then by their speech; identity discloses itself through an outward trace.
تَعْرِفُ فِى وُجُوهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ٱلْمُنكَرَ makes rejection recognizable in faces precisely while God's verses are recited, supplying the evil face-trace in the section's dictionary image.
تَعْرِفُ فِى وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ ٱلنَّعِيمِ makes bliss recognizable in faces, supplying the good face-trace paired with the section's good-or-evil reading.
The people on the Heights يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّۢا بِسِيمَاهُمْ, recognizing every group by its marks; the sign visibly distinguishes belonging and fate.
The people on the Heights address men whom they know بِسِيمَاهُمْ; this continuation shows a mark identifying particular persons even before their final admission is announced.
تَعْرِفُهُم بِسِيمَاهُمْ directs the giver to recognize the restrained poor by their sign despite their refusal to ask, so an unspoken condition is read from a trace.
لَوَّاحَةٌ لِّلْبَشَرِ describes Hell as scorching or altering the skin; it is the fire-mark on hide made into eschatological judgment.
The pagans invent livestock restrictions and animals عَلَيْهَا ٱفْتِرَآءً عَلَيْهِ over which God's name is not mentioned; the absent name exposes a counterfeit claim of ownership and consecration.
Each community receives a rite so that God's name may be mentioned over the livestock He provided; name, provider-owner, and marked ritual animal form the section's scene.
Eating what God's name has been mentioned over makes the name a practical sign of lawful dedication, close to the section's ownership-mark reading of اسم.
The prohibition on eating what God's name was not mentioned over draws a boundary between two allegiances; an animal without the true owner's name becomes a site of satanic dispute.
God owns the beautiful names and the hearer is told to leave those who distort them; this directly supports hearing “glorify your Lord's name” as keeping His identifying name pure.
فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ repeats the command to glorify the Lord's name immediately after the passage makes kindled fire a reminder, bringing the section's name and fire together.
After the lodging of Hellfire in 56:94, فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ again places the purified Lord-name beside the alternative fire-sign.
فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ is the same stance and nearly the same command as the section's opening; the name is something actively kept in glorification.
لَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ is joined in the same ayah to all creation glorifying Him, directly uniting the Lord's names with tasbih.
ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ makes the Lord's name the sign under which recitation begins, expressing action conducted in the owner's allegiance.
وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا joins remembering the Lord's name to exclusive devotion, making the named owner distinguish the servant's allegiance.
وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ states the section's lexicographic claim almost verbatim: the sought Lord is the Lord and owner of every thing.
وَعَلَـٰمَـٰتٍۢ وَبِٱلنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ uses the knowledge-root for distinguishing landmarks; a readable mark makes direction knowable exactly as the section's root definition says.
God says He left from Lot's settlement ءَايَةًۢ بَيِّنَةً, a clear surviving sign; the destroyed place itself becomes the remainder from which judgment is read.
The ruined settlement lies بِسَبِيلٍۢ مُّقِيمٍ, on an enduring road; it explains how the discerning readers of 15:75 can encounter and read the city's remaining trace.
وَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِم مُّصْبِحِينَ tells the audience that they pass Lot's ruins by morning, turning the vanished people into a repeatedly visible trace.
Passing the ruins by night is followed by أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ, demanding inference from the scene just as the section's mutawassim reads meaning from remains.
أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ is what the soon-to-be-branded man calls the revelations; it makes his treatment of the “first” records the identifying act answered by 68:16.
The command not to obey every habitual swearer and contemptible man begins the portrait whose traits culminate in the brand of 68:16; the addressee must read character before following it.
هَمَّازٍۢ مَّشَّآءٍۭ بِنَمِيمٍ supplies the slander and tale-bearing traits of the bearer branded in 68:16, making the punishment an identifying summary of lived character.
The dawn blast that seizes Lot's people supplies the audible catastrophe whose physical aftermath the mutawassim reads in 15:75.
Turning the city upside down and raining baked-clay stones creates the ruined trace read in 15:75; this ayah contributes the destruction itself.
The magicians say لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَـٰتِ and refuse to prefer Pharaoh over clear signs and their Creator, reversing the choice of the nearer life.
وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ follows the refusal to prefer Pharaoh, matching the section's “the Hereafter is better and more lasting” and showing what correct preference leaves one loyal to.
Hell is where the criminal لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ, the same neither-dead-nor-alive fire consequence that follows the section's worldly preference.
وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا repeats the section's preference almost word for word, making the chosen world the decisive identifier of the transgressor.
فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ states the fire outcome of 79:38's worldly preference, completing the same preference-to-fire movement as this image.
وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ reverses self-serving preference: the Helpers prefer others despite need, so the same root can leave a mark of generosity rather than attachment to الدنيا.
God denies instituting the named livestock classes baḥīrah, sāʾibah, waṣīlah, and ḥām; it rejects humanly invented animal markings as claims about divine ownership.

Immediately after the marked horses and worldly adornments of 3:14, the hearer is asked whether he wants news of something better; the contrast supplies the right valuation of the branded-animal scene.
Joseph's brothers bring his shirt with false blood, manufacturing a misleading bodily trace; it is the boundary case showing that a visible أثر can be forged and must be read truthfully.
The alleged gods are only names coined by people and their fathers without God's authority; an empty name is the opposite of the true Lord's ownership-sign.
The idols are again called mere names coined without divine authority, exposing a name that falsely assigns sacred identity rather than revealing its true owner.
The promised angels are مُسَوِّمِينَ, marked or marking according to the reading; the disputed sense still extends the w-s-m identity-sign from livestock to a divinely distinguished host.
Whenever the condemned person's skins are burned, they are exchanged for other skins to taste punishment; the branded hide expands into a whole skin made to bear fire's consequence.
Hearing, sight, and skins testify to what their owners did, so the hide itself discloses the life attached to it, like the section's mark that identifies its bearer.
The condemned ask their skins why they testified, and the skins name God as the one who made them speak; the body's surface becomes a truthful owner-linked record rather than a mute hide.
Tongues, hands, and feet testify to what people used to do; conduct leaves the person bodily identifiable even without an external brand.
Every person's طَـٰٓئِرَهُ is fastened to his neck and his record is brought out, giving each person an attached, individualized sign of what he chose and did.
The person who takes desire as a god is sealed on hearing and heart; the governing preference becomes a divine mark upon the chooser's faculties.
كَتَبَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْإِيمَـٰنَ makes faith an inscription in the hearts of God's party, a positive inward counterpart to the fire-brand and the rust of earning.
The Samaritan takes a handful مِنْ أَثَرِ ٱلرَّسُولِ and casts it into the calf; a physical trace is misappropriated to manufacture a false object of allegiance.
Moses and his servant return عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا, following their own tracks; this supplies the literal ground-trace by which a path and its walkers are recognized.
فَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِ رَحْمَتِ ٱللَّهِ asks the reader to recognize God's mercy from its effects on dead earth, a benevolent version of knowing an owner through what His act leaves behind.
Earlier peoples left greater ءَاثَارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ, yet their ruins survive as evidence after the people vanish; the remainder identifies a lost power and its judgment.
The audience is sent through the earth to see the outcome of stronger peoples with greater ءَاثَارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ; trace-reading becomes moral recognition from ruins.
The repeated command to travel and see peoples with more آثار in the earth makes surviving works into marks whose owners and fate can still be known.
The idolaters claim وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ, treating ancestral tracks as guidance; inherited preference leaves a path by which the present community is identified.
وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم مُّقْتَدُونَ repeats that allegiance as following forebears' traces, showing a mark transmitted by imitation rather than received from the true Lord.
The condemned found their fathers astray; it identifies the owners of the bad tracks into which they hurry in 37:70.
فَهُمْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ pictures people rushing along their ancestors' traces, making a chosen allegiance recognizable as a followed trail toward punishment.
Moses says his people are عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى, on his trace; the word marks a relation of following and belonging, the relational remainder in the section's أثر definition.
Jesus is sent عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم after the prophets, turning أثر into faithful succession: a prior bearer leaves a line that another follows.
Messengers and Jesus are sent عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم, again using traces for a continuing relation across absent generations rather than a merely visible footprint.
لَقَدْ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا makes preference God's act of distinguishing Joseph from his brothers, a different agent and moral direction from humans preferring the nearer life.
The eye must not reach toward worldly splendor because وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ; the Lord-owner's provision is better and more lasting than the preferred display.
Worldly gifts are temporary enjoyment and adornment, while what is with God is خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ, restating the section's valuation of what passes against what remains.
What people are given is enjoyment of worldly life, while what is with God is خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ for believers; enduring ownership supplies the criterion of preference.
مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقٍ draws the section's أثر-as-remainder boundary explicitly: human possessions vanish, while what belongs with God remains.
كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ states the disappearance side of the section's contrast between passing preference and a surviving remainder.
وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ names the Lord as what remains after all earthly bearers pass, grounding permanence in the owner rather than in the temporary mark.
Worldly wealth and children are adornment, while lasting righteous deeds are better with the Lord; what one does leaves the better remainder than what one displays.
ٱلْبَـٰقِيَـٰتُ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ are better with the Lord in reward and return, giving the section's enduring أثر an ethical content.
The rebuke asks whether people are content with worldly life instead of the Hereafter and calls its enjoyment slight; it names the valuation behind the section's marked preference.
Those who يَسْتَحِبُّونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا عَلَى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ enact the same preference without the أثر verb, and their obstruction shows the conduct that choice produces.
بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ restates the attraction to the immediate life as the controlling love by which the audience is identified.
وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ gives the other side of that preference: choosing the immediate necessarily leaves the lasting life behind.
إِنَّ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ يُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ identifies a people by love of the immediate and neglect of a heavy coming day, matching the section's claim that preference marks the chooser.
Whoever desires the immediate life receives a measured share and then is assigned Hell; the desired world culminates in the fire-sign attached to that choice.
Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it has effort gratefully recognized; the alternative preference leaves an accepted rather than fiery أثر.
The one who gathers and counts wealth supplies the worldly attachment whose eventual fire reaches inward in 104:6-7.
نَارُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُوقَدَةُ is the divine fire awaiting the wealth-counter, connecting a preferred possession to the Lord's contrary mark.
The fire تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى ٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةِ, reaching the hearts; the outward brand becomes an inward disclosure of what the person loved.
The question about the fire people kindle opens the immediate context of the glorify-the-name command in 56:74, placing ordinary visible fire before the Lord's name.
God says He made that fire تَذْكِرَةً, a reminder or sign; it therefore already functions as something from which its maker and a greater fire are recognized before 56:74.
تَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ supplies the fire fate directly before the renewed command to glorify the Lord's name in 56:96, reproducing the image's two possible signs.
The divine titles ٱلْقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَـٰمُ clear the named Lord of defect immediately before 59:24 joins His beautiful names to universal glorification.
سُبْحَـٰنَ رَبِّكَ ... عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ is an explicit command-formula of keeping the Lord free of defective descriptions, the sense the section hears in purifying His mark.
تَبَـٰرَكَ ٱسْمُ رَبِّكَ closes the surah by blessing the Lord's name itself, treating the name as the bearer of His majesty and honor.
وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ commands regular remembrance of the Lord's name, the positive sign of allegiance opposed to being known by fire.
The sacrificial animals and their garlands must not be violated; the garland is a visible, non-burning livestock sign that marks the animal as consecrated to God.
Honoring God's شعائر is said to come from the piety of hearts; the outward belonging-sign on rites and animals is traced back to an inward mark.
Hunters are told to mention God's name over what trained animals catch, using the name to identify the lawful relation among owner, animal, and food.
Prayer, sacrifice, life, and death are declared لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ; the whole self and its animal offering are assigned to the named Lord-owner.
God teaches Adam the names and asks that the named things be identified, giving اسم the practical work of distinguishing one thing from another.
Calling adopted sons by their fathers preserves true lineage and belonging; it parallels the section's animal brand as a sign by which stock and owner are not confused.
Joseph proposes that the direction of the torn shirt be read as evidence, turning a physical remainder into a discriminator between truth and accusation.
A rear tear would mark Joseph as truthful and his accuser as lying; this ayah states explicitly how one trace distinguishes moral identities.
When the husband sees the shirt torn from behind, he reads the trace and reaches judgment; it is the concrete act of tawassum without the root.
Those who lied about God appear on Resurrection with faces blackened; the lie about the true Lord becomes an identifying face-mark.
Some faces whiten and others blacken on the Day, making opposed allegiances legible on their bearers before punishment is pronounced.
Those whose faces whiten enter God's mercy permanently, supplying the good visible sign opposite the darkened face of 3:106.
The doers of good receive the best, and neither darkness nor abasement covers their faces; their faces are protected from the evil mark.
Evil earners have faces covered as though by pieces of dark night and are identified as companions of the Fire; deed, face-trace, and fire meet.
Faces on that Day are bright, beginning a paired portrait in which inward outcome is readable on the face.
Other faces have dust upon them, giving the contrary group a visible residue or mark.
The bearers of the darkened faces are identified as disbelieving transgressors, completing the inference from facial sign to moral identity.
Fire scorches their faces, making punishment itself write the condemned identity onto the same facial surface on which the section reads marks.
The calf is made to sink into their hearts through disbelief; the chosen object of worship leaves an inward attachment by which the people are known.
